Hi Ellen / Tom —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Private VPC deployment with strict egress controls (air-gapped or limited outbound)
- Customer-managed control plane (or an option for a private control plane hosted in Acme infra)
- KMS/HSM integration for key management and no plaintext token egress
- Networking: support for PrivateLink/VPN/Direct Connect-style peering, ability to run inference nodes with no internet egress
- Perf targets: sub-200ms median token latency for text-gen workloads at 32 token windows; predictable throughput for batch scoring

High-level Redwood approach (how we differ vs hyperscalers/managed inference APIs):
- Private deployment modes: we can run a private control plane inside your VPC or optionally a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment (control plane sync via an ops-only jumpbox).
- Networking flexibility: support for AWS PrivateLink / GCP VPC Peering / Azure Private Link patterns. Inference nodes can be provisioned in your subnet with no NAT gateway; only the control plane needs an authenticated control channel when not air-gapped.
- Security: SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and per-request telemetry. We keep no customer model artifacts in our hosted control plane when a private control plane is selected.
- Cost/perf: our runtime is optimized for throughput and cost: batching + prefix caching, model/quantization profiles tuned for your LLMs. We’ll share a competitor comparison brief attached.

Proposed next tests / POC scope:
1) Networking validation: we run a short connectivity test to validate routing, required ports, and egress restrictions (we’ll provide a checklist).
2) Control plane handshake: validate the private control plane bootstrap in your environment (or establish the ops jumpbox workflow for air-gapped).
3) Perf sanity test: run a lightweight latency/throughput run using a small subset of production prompts to validate median token latency and warm KV cache behavior.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf (competitive bullets), networking-checklist.xlsx (ports and CIDR expectations), soc2-evidence-summary.pdf

Next steps I propose:
- Can your infra/security folks review the networking checklist? I can set a short 30-min call with our infra engineer (Camila) to walk through specifics.
- Tentative window for POC: June 22–26. Does that work on your side?

If useful I can also include a short matrix comparing required customer changes for Redwood Private vs GCP Vertex AI / AWS Bedrock / self-hosted runtimes.

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Ellen / Tom — thanks — answering inline below and proposing concrete next steps.

1) Outbound connectivity from inference nodes (heartbeat):
- For the strictest air-gapped mode: no outbound connectivity is required. We support a fully air-gapped deployment where inference nodes only communicate within your isolated network and model artifacts are staged via signed bundles pushed from the ops jumpbox. The control plane can be run as a customer-managed service inside your VPC or physically on-prem.
- For the private control plane in your VPC (non-airgapped): inference nodes still do not require general internet access. We use an authenticated control channel between the customer-managed control plane and the nodes; that channel can be configured over private peering or PrivateLink. Heartbeats and telemetry are sent to your control plane endpoint only. No data is echoed back to Redwood hosted services unless you choose to forward telemetry.

2) Components hosted by Redwood vs customer-managed:
- Customer-managed control plane option: all control plane services (auth, routing, rollouts, audit logs) run in your VPC under your account. Redwood provides container images, deployment manifests, and a bootstrap operator. We do not store model artifacts or keys in our hosted control plane in this mode.
- Hosted (Redwood-managed) option: control plane runs in Redwood cloud and communicates with inference nodes; this is the fastest onboarding path but not air-gapped.

3) Ops-only jumpbox sync for air-gapped deployments:
- We provide a signed artifact export flow (bundle signed by Redwood and verifiable by your HSM) that your ops team pulls via the jumpbox. The process can be scripted to run nightly or manually triggered; we will provide the automation scripts and an acceptance checklist.

4) Cost comparison vs hyperscalers (high level):
- Hyperscalers often price as managed infra + endpoint tax; for large steady-state inference we typically see Redwood Private come in lower on per-token cost once batching & caching optimizations are applied, because you pay mostly for the compute and we optimize kernels and quantization. Exact delta depends on instance family and utilization. I’ve attached a short brief with ballpark comparisons (redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf). We can run a TCO estimate once you share target QPS and instance preferences.

Proposed next steps (concrete):
- 30-min networking walkthrough Thursday 6/17 10:00–10:30 PT with Camila (infra engineer) to go through networking-checklist.xlsx. Camila — are you available?
- If that looks good, we’ll schedule a 2-day POC (connectivity + perf checks) starting June 22. I’ll send a one-page POC plan to your team after the call.

If you’d like I can also outline the competitor differences in a simple table (we’ll call out where hyperscalers require additional managed connectors or don't support air-gapped bundles).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.
